title: Projectome input count did not predict the shared dimensionality of single-neuron activity in 47 larval zebrafish brain regions after signal-quality controls (22 fish)
abstract: Question: in the larval zebrafish brain, does the diversity of the anatomical inputs of a region predict the shared dimensionality of the single-neuron activity in that region? Data: processed whole-brain two-photon calcium imaging of 22 larvae (Legare et al. 2025, CC BY 4.0; about 600 s of spontaneous activity at 1 volume/s) and the source authors' directed mapZebrain projectome (70 regions). Method (pre-registered): for 47 regions with at least 200 ROIs in at least 11 fish, shared-variance component analysis (SVCA) on 50 random sets of 100 ROIs; outcome = participation ratio (PR) of reliable covariance; partial Spearman rho across regions with controls for in-strength, volume, ROI signal quality, brightness and ROI spread; region bootstrap. Results: input diversity did not predict SVCA PR (rho -0.18, 95% CI -0.56 to +0.25). None of 16 pre-registered variants had a CI above zero. A raw positive link (+0.25, positive in 19 of 22 fish) followed signal quality: regions with more inputs had noisier ROIs (rho -0.47) and fewer shared components above a noise floor (-0.52). A flatter noisy spectrum raises the PR. A pre-registered functional input diversity measure (PR of the SC-weighted correlations among source regions) beat a distance-matched input permutation null (+0.43 vs null mean +0.20, p = 0.019), but not after control for source signal quality (p = 0.35). Exploratory, post hoc: regions whose input sources were less correlated with each other had fewer detectable shared components (p = 0.002 against the null) and lower internal correlation (p = 0.021), after that control. Limitations: noisy 1 Hz nuclear-indicator single-ROI signals (median within-region r 0.008), coarse regions as the unit of inference, nearly collinear input count, diversity and strength, and a sparse projectome from other animals. Code, hashes, derived region data and figures are included.

A: partial Spearman rho across regions with 95% region-bootstrap intervals for the pre-registered test and its variants (blue: input measures; orange: output measure; gray: other outcomes). B: per-fish partial rho (blue odd, green even fish); the black lines are means.

Functional input diversity (FID) against 1,000 distance-matched input permutations (exploratory null B). The PR result disappears after control for source signal quality (A, B); the negative links to detectable components and mean correlation stay (C, D).
